summary:
Baymax is an onboard AI health companion developed by the ASTRA VITAL team for NASA Space Apps 2026. It aims to protect astronauts' physical and mental health during long-duration space missions, especially when communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable.

The system provides continuous health and environmental monitoring, rule-based emergency detection, AI-powered first-aid guidance grounded in medical reference documents, radiation hazard mapping, and isolation detection. It also supports astronauts' mental well-being through family messages, photos, videos, and voice-pattern monitoring.

Baymax uses an offline-first architecture that stores events and reports locally and synchronizes them with Mission Control when connectivity returns. Flight surgeons can remotely update medical protocols and safety thresholds through Update Packs.

Its AI layer analyses health data, detects abnormal patterns, and generates automated reports to support informed decisions. The system combines AI assistance with auditable safety rules to ensure that emergency decisions never depend on an AI language model.

Baymax aims to make space missions safer, more autonomous, and more supportive for astronauts, with potential applications in other remote and isolated environments on Earth.
